races.title: State Assembly, District 43
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Celeste Rodriguez
cands.bio: Democrat representing California's 43rd Assembly District (eastern San Fernando Valley) since December 2024. Former San Fernando mayor and city councilmember. Previously deputy director of Community Development Strategies in the Los Angeles mayor's office. Holds a USC master's in social work and an SDSU economics degree.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and Sierra Club Angeles Chapter.
Her campaign site lists endorsements from U.S. Sen. Alex Padilla, Rep. Luz Rivas, former Rep. Tony Cárdenas and Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass.

cands.gaps: Her birthplace is not stated in the pages I could read. I found no documented stance on data centers or development. I found no specific bills, actions or statements from her on homestead property taxes, investor or foreign land buying, immigration enforcement or H-1B, policing, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. Her campaign site speaks only in general terms about protecting families from being torn apart and investing in education. Ballotpedia's list of bills she sponsored did not display, and she did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. I found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages I read.

local.label: Roots 90: Her campaign site says she and her siblings were raised in the Northeast Valley and attended James Monroe High School in North Hills; she still lives in San Fernando, and no birthplace is stated in the text I read.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since December 2024; San Fernando city councilmember from 2020 and mayor from December 2022; earlier deputy director of Community Development Strategies in the Los Angeles mayor's office, running anti-poverty and economic programs.
qual.why: She has prior legislative service in the Assembly, local elected office as councilmember and mayor, and a policy and program-management career in city government.

cands.name: Ricardo Benitez
cands.bio: Republican who has run repeatedly for the California State Assembly and State Senate, most recently in Assembly District 43 in 2026. He was a plaintiff in a 2020 lawsuit against Gov. Newsom over a state immigrant aid program. No elected office is documented.

endorsements.text: Voter-guide recommendations and endorsements listed for 2026: Reform California, April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide, and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Ricardo Benitez was born or raised, when he came to California, or his occupation and work history. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020 or 2026, and the sources hold no campaign website or platform statements. We found no documented positions on data centers, development, property taxes, immigration enforcement, guns, abortion, schools or policing, and no documented actions on those topics. The only record of him taking action is his role as a plaintiff in the April 2020 lawsuit over Newsom's immigrant aid program, and the lawsuit's outcome is not covered.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: No occupation or work history appears in the sources. The record shows only repeated unsuccessful campaigns for Assembly (2012, 2018, 2020, 2026) and State Senate (2014), and no elected office.
qual.why: The sources do not state a career or any office held, so a job-fit score can't be established.
